title: The Greatest Commandment
summary: What God commands is always what's best for us. A divided heart is full of anxiety. Loving Jesus with our whole heart makes us whole.
exhortation: What God commands is always what's best for us. Jesus knows that a divided heart is full of anxiety, fear, doubt and frustration. Loving him makes us whole and gives us our true purpose. In loving Jesus with all our heart, soul and mind, we find peace.

So how do we love Jesus? What do we actually do? First, we obey his command to love others. We live in a sinful, fallen world, so that can be hard at times. But he commands us to love others, to love his people and his church. Our hearts often lie to us and say that selfishness and taking care of ourselves first will make us happy. Nothing could be further from the truth. I think we've all experienced that loving others gives us a whole heart, meaning and purpose.

And when Jesus commands us to love God with all our heart, soul and mind, it's like telling a child to love ice cream or a surfer to love the ocean. Jesus is so amazing, so lovely, so worthy of all our affection, that it's almost silly to call it a command. It's what we were made for. Loving Jesus is joy to our souls and peace for our hearts.

Thankfully, Jesus has given us the Holy Spirit, because our hearts are prone to sin and prone to wander. We need his help this morning. I'm sure we're distracted, with worry in the background and anxiety creeping in. So, Holy Spirit, come and fill us, and fix our eyes on Jesus, who is altogether lovely and worthy of our praise.
prayer: Lord, it isn't enough that we know about you. It isn't even enough to know the Scriptures well. Even our enemy knows the Scriptures. You must be our greatest delight, the one we desire above all else, the one who captures our affection.

Stir up our hearts with great love. Give us the gift of wonder at being saved, gratitude for your kindness, and amazement at your mercy. Whatever our background, we all came from the same place, dead in our sin, and you rescued us. May we remember, be filled with gratitude, and have our hearts quickened to love you totally and completely.
